title: Nightcap micro-eval — oddities and todo
content:
Evening brain-dump after the late microbench runs. Not polished — notes to self and quick TODOs.

Context
- Goal: hunt down weird latency/quality regressions seen on quantized 4-bit variant (q4_neo) when prefix lengths > 512 and KV cache reuse is enabled.
- Environment: dedicated dev pool (g4dn-sim), runtime build: serving-runtime@pr-8342, ffwd kernels enabled.
- Quick summary: baseline throughput looks fine, but intermittent token-stall spikes (~120–300ms extra per-token) on ~1% of requests when cache reuse flag is on. Those spikes correlate with requests that have early-bird re-rollbacks (canary fallback to fp16).

Raw observations (logs/snippets)
- Run IDs: nightcap-20260327-r1..r6. Attachments in linked artifacts branch.
- Example trace excerpt (simplified):
  * request: model=q4_neo, seq=2048, prefix=1024, kv_reuse=true
  * step 438: kvcache flush->realloc path taken (timing +220ms)
  * fallback: route->fp16-variant (routed by smart-routing policy)
- Pattern: majority of spikes when the prefix contains many repeated short tokens (e.g., long lists / copy-pasted JSON). Hypothesis: attention pattern degeneracy + quantized kernel boundary triggers extra buffer copy.

Quick prompt set used (small reproducible set)
1) "Summarize the following JSON: {large nested object with repeating keys}" (prefix with heavily repeated keys)
2) "Rewrite this long bulleted list into prose" (list length 300–600 tokens)
3) "Continue this legal contract clause" (examines long-range attention)

Quality checks ran
- Perplexity (on small eval set): q4_neo ppl ~ 1.12x fp16 baseline on average, but p95 of perplexity shows spikes when token-stall occurs.
- Repetition rate: tiny increase (~0.6%) in repeated 3-grams for q4_neo in these corner cases.
- Human spot-check: a few completions truncated mid-sentence when stall -> fallback occurred.

Hypotheses to test (prioritized)
- H1: Kernel boundary condition when sequence length crosses internal block size causes an intermediate copy + sync that isn't properly asynchronous on the quantized path. Repro: craft inputs that force crossing at same token index repeatedly.
- H2: KV cache reference counting bug leads to temporary double-free/lock contention causing a short stall observable in CPU side. Check allocator logs.
- H3: Smart routing policy's capacity probe misinterprets a transient latency as pressure and triggers fallback prematurely. Verify routing trace correlation.

Mini experiments to run (next 48h)
- E1: Add microbench that synthesizes repeated-key JSON with controlled block boundary offsets (shift start by 1..64 tokens). Measure p50/p95 token latency and kernel metrics. Tag run names: dor-nightcap-e1..e4.
- E2: Toggle kv_reuse=false for same inputs and compare. If stall disappears, narrow down to cache path.
- E3: Instrument allocator with brief high-freq sampling (100Hz) during runs to capture short-lived contention.

Immediate TODOs (prio order)
- [ ] Wire PR-8342 branch with extra debug toggles: KVCHECK=1, ASYNC_COPY=0, LOG_TIMER=1. (Mila to review)
- [ ] Create small reproducer harness in serving-runtime/tests/microbench (no infra dependency) — target 1-minute run. (me)
- [ ] Post short summary + one failing trace to #eng-quant with link to branch and Jira (JIRA-ML-1029). (Noah will ping)
- [ ] Try same input on dedicated-prod-sim region to confirm not dev-pool-specific.

Questions / open things
- Is the fallback happening inside the router before inference begins, or mid-inference? Trace shows both patterns, need clearer classification.
- Could the tokenizer splitting of repeated tokens matter for internal block alignment? Worth trying consistent tokenization variants (byte-level vs spm).
- Does quantization-stability degrade with repeated keys because of narrow-value distribution? Might be a numerical stability edge case.

Notes to self (quick snippets)
- If reproducer needs <10s to trigger, can escalate to SRE to look at perf counters.
- Remember to tag runs with exact commit hash + kernel flags.
- Avoid dropping large raw logs in Drive — put compressed traces in artifacts bucket and link.

Scratchpad commands (for later)
- run microbench: ./tools/run_microbench --model q4_neo --input tests/repro/json_repeat_1024.txt --kv-reuse=true --tag dor-nightcap-rx
- collect debug: ./tools/collect_debug --run dor-nightcap-rx --out s3://redwood-artifacts/nightcap/

Nightcap wrap-up thoughts
- This feels like a narrow buffer-sync/async mismatch that only surfaces with quantized kernels and very repetitive token patterns. If we can create a deterministic reproducer, we can either patch the driver to avoid the sync or adjust router to avoid fallbacks mid-sequence.
- Keep scope limited: target a minimal reproducer and one fix in runtime; don't try to change routing logic until root cause identified.

Random brain-storm (for later)
- Add a fuzz harness that cycles block alignment jitter across many inputs — might catch this and other off-by-one boundary issues.
- Quick metric to add in Console: percent of requests that have mid-inference variant switch (this would have surfaced this faster).

End of dump. Will re-organize tomorrow morning, link PR and Jira once I have the reproducer run links.

-- Dorian
